gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the kits' cycle-life ratings can't be compared: Jackery rates the Explorer 1000 v2 at 4,000 cycles to 70% capacity, EcoFlow's US store rates the DELTA 3 Classic at '10 years' with no cycle count, and BLUETTI says only 'over 3,000 cycles' for the Elite 30 V2 without saying what capacity is left at that point; also, the Elite 30 V2's '1,500 W' is a resistive-only 'lifting' mode, not a surge rating.
standout_why: I read powerstationgearlab.com (cited). It gives no cycle life, no capacity endpoint and no surge for Jackery, EcoFlow or BLUETTI, only 'up to 500W solar input'. I read flowersofvice.com (cited). It gives no cycle counts and no endpoint, so it doesn't compare 70% with 80%. Its only surge figures are Jackery's 3,000 W and the AC180's 2,700 W, and it labels EcoFlow's X-Boost as an output figure, not a surge. urbangridbackup.com (cited, rank 1) would not open: WebFetch failed on its certificate and curl was blocked in this session, so I could not check it. ChatGPT's own answers compare Wh and AC watts only. Our current page has no cycle-life or surge column.
decides: This confirms the pick rather than changing it. The DELTA 3 Classic kit stays the 1 kWh pick, and EcoFlow's US store sells it for $669, less than the $729 Best Buy card ChatGPT showed. On durability, the page should say the makers' numbers can't be compared, not rank them, because only Jackery names an endpoint and it is the looser 70%. For the compact tier, the Elite 30 V2 is a 600 W continuous unit, and its 1,500 W 'lifting' figure covers only kettles and heaters, not motor start-up. The Anker C300 is 300 W continuous with a 600 W surge, so neither compact kit runs a mini-fridge as well as a 1 kWh unit does.

findings.label: Cycle life and its endpoint
findings.source_title: Jackery Explorer 1000 v2 Review – BackupPowerHub (Andrew Harrington, updated 2026-09-30)
findings.note: Harrington quotes Jackery's rating as keeping '70% or more of its original capacity after 4,000 full charge/discharge cycles'. Jackery's own page returned HTTP 429 every time I tried it, so I'm citing the named reviewer's spec table. The endpoint is 70%, while the others are 80% or unstated, so 4,000 here is a looser claim than the same number elsewhere.
